title: CtlPlan
description: What a mutation WOULD do — the 200 body of every mutating operation called with `dry_run: true`, and the thing a client must have seen before it executes. `plan_hash` = sha256 over the canonical JSON of `{op, tenant, args_redacted, registry_generation, doctor_findings_sha256, steps[].{kind, target, args_sha256}, schema_version}`; the execute call carries the same request, the daemon recomputes the hash AFTER taking the locks, and a mismatch is 409 `plan_stale` (the registry moved, a finding changed, an argument differs). `requires_confirm: true` means the execute call must also carry `confirm: <confirm_value>` — the tenant name for tenant ops (like the CLI's `--yes-destructive <name>`), `gateway` or `settings` otherwise — or it is 428 `confirm_required`. Previews inside `would_write` are redacted and capped at 64 KiB.

doctor.description: The op-scoped doctor run this plan was computed against — same shape as `GET /v1/doctor?tenant=&op=`. A `red` status here means the execute call will be 409 `doctor_red` unless the findings change.

targets.description: What the step acts on — unit names, instance names, collection names, paths (redacted).

mode.description: Octal file mode as written, e.g. `0660`.

preview.description: Redacted content, ≤ 64 KiB; null when the file is binary or the content is a secret (e.g. `secrets.env`).

argv.description: Absolute program then arguments — the ctl never runs a shell.
